text: On that day seven women will seize a single man and say, "We will eat our own bread and wear our own clothes—only let us be called by your name. Take away our disgrace."
On that day the Branch of the LORD will be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the land will be the pride and splendor of those in Israel who survive.

versions.text: On that day the Branch of the LORD will be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the land will be the pride and splendor of the survivors of Israel.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew לִפְלֵיטַת ("for the remnant/survivors") marks the beneficiaries, not possessors; "for those in Israel who survive" is more accurate and reads more naturally aloud than the ambiguous genitive "of the survivors of Israel."

text: And everyone who is left in Zion, who remains in Jerusalem, will be called holy—everyone recorded for life in Jerusalem.
When the Lord has washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion and rinsed away the bloodstains from the midst of Jerusalem by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning,

versions.text: For the Lord will wash away the filth of the daughters of Zion and cleanse the bloodstains from Jerusalem's midst by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning.
versions.explanation: The particle אִם here functions temporally/conditionally ("when"), setting up the condition that leads into the promise of verse 5 ("Then the LORD will create..."). Rendering it as "For" turns the clause into an independent statement and loses the logical link with the following verse.

versions.text: When the Lord has washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion and cleansed the bloodstains from Jerusalem's midst by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning,
versions.explanation: "from Jerusalem's midst" is a compressed possessive that reads awkwardly aloud; "from the midst of Jerusalem" preserves the Hebrew מִקִּרְבָּהּ and flows better in oral reading. "Rinsed away" also renders יָדִיחַ (to rinse/flush) a bit more concretely and avoids repeating the general idea of "washed" from the first clause.

text: Then the LORD will create over all of Mount Zion and over her assemblies a cloud by day and smoke, and the brightness of a flaming fire by night; for over all the glory there will be a canopy.
And there will be a shelter, a shade by day from the heat, a refuge and a hiding place from storm and rain.

versions.text: It will be a shelter, a shade by day from the heat, a refuge and a hiding place from storm and rain.
versions.explanation: The pronoun "It" has no clear antecedent when the verse is read aloud on its own; the Hebrew simply states that a booth/shelter will exist, so an existential construction is clearer and smoother for oral reading.
